title: Evidence-Grounded Constraint Schemas Do Not Improve Medical LLM Guardrails on LiveMedBench

contributions.purpose: Determines whether structured constraint representations outperform unstructured ones for medical LLM guardrails.
contributions.mechanism: Controlled comparison of structured JSON schema guardrails versus plain-text checklist guardrails, holding constraint content and evidence quotes identical across 3-pass pipelines.
contributions.evaluation: Evaluated on 500 constraint-salient medical cases from LiveMedBench with case-specific weighted rubrics.
contributions.source_quote: A controlled comparison of structured JSON schema guardrails versus plain-text checklist guardrails on 500 constraint-salient medical cases from LiveMedBench.

contributions.purpose: Establishes that multi-pass guardrail pipelines do not improve over a well-designed single-pass baseline.
contributions.mechanism: Tests 9 guardrail variants (6 optimization variants across 3 pipeline architectures) against a single-pass baseline with a strong constraint-aware prompt.
contributions.evaluation: Single-pass baseline outperforms all 9 variants; the proposed schema guardrail scores -0.013 below baseline (0.522 vs 0.535) on constraint-focused rubric, checklist scores -0.024.
contributions.source_quote: A robust negative result: the single-pass baseline outperforms all 9 guardrail variants tested, with the proposed schema guardrail scoring -0.013 below baseline on constraint-focused rubric.

contributions.purpose: Explains why constraint-extraction guardrails degrade performance.
contributions.mechanism: Criteria-level analysis identifying a 'cautious bias' failure mechanism where constraint extraction causes models to omit correct medical content while trying to avoid violations.
contributions.evaluation: Guardrail pipelines lose 116 positive criteria while only avoiding 55 negative criteria, a net performance degradation.
contributions.source_quote: Identification of "cautious bias" as the failure mechanism: guardrail pipelines lose 116 positive criteria while only avoiding 55 negative criteria, resulting in net performance degradation.

contributions.purpose: Gives practitioners deployment guidance for constraint handling in medical LLM systems.
contributions.mechanism: Cost-effectiveness comparison of single-pass prompting versus multi-pass guardrail pipelines for Qwen3-14B.
contributions.evaluation: A well-designed single-pass prompt is both more effective and 2.4-2.7x more efficient than multi-pass guardrail pipelines on LiveMedBench.
contributions.source_quote: Practical guidance: for Qwen3-14B on LiveMedBench, a well-designed single-pass prompt is more effective and 2.4-2.7x more efficient than multi-pass guardrail pipelines.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Self-refinement methods (Madaan et al., 2023) have shown promise for iterative improvement, while structured outputs enable reliable constraint extraction. Checklists have been proposed for LLM alignment (Viswanathan et al., 2025), suggesting that explicit constraint representations could help models avoid violations. We hypothesize that evidence-grounded constraint schemas ... should improve constraint handling compared to unstructured approaches.
Condition B (Checklist Guardrail). A 3-pass pipeline inspired by self-refinement approaches (Madaan et al., 2023)

Prior work on medical LLM evaluation identifies Contextual Neglect and Integration Failure (CNIF) as a dominant failure mode ... (Yan et al., 2026). We investigate whether explicit constraint extraction and structured revision can reduce such failures.

notes: Explicit negative-result paper: the proposed evidence-grounded constraint schema guardrail (and all 9 guardrail variants) fail to beat the single-pass baseline. All contributions are findings/analysis rather than a new method. Paper carries an automated-research-system generation warning.
